The $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ on the curve $y={e}^{x}\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ that is closest to the point $(1,0)$ satisfies the equation

$$
2x-2+=0.
$$

 
What is the missing expression?

The $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ on the curve $y={log}_{2}⁡x$  that is closest to the origin (as shown above) satisfies the equation 

$$
2x+=0.
$$

 

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(0,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x,y) & =(x-0)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{log}_{2}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x+2{log}_{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} & =0 \\ 2x+\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$
